tools.description: Read-only. Lists the exchanges FormNET's proxy recorded, newest last, without headers or bodies: method, URL, status, kind, sizes, timing and the process that sent it. Use it to see what a program sent, to find a flow id for get_flow, or to poll for new traffic by passing the last_seq of the previous answer as since. Filters are those of the FormNET API (host, domain, kind, client, q, since, pending); limit defaults to 25 and returns the newest matches. Kind refused lists programs that rejected FormNET's certificate.

client.description: Only flows from a client address starting with this ip:port prefix, as list_flows shows it in client.

domain.description: Only flows whose host belongs to this registrable domain, such as example.com (it covers its subdomains).

host.description: Only flows to this host: an exact name such as api.example.com, or a *.suffix pattern such as *.example.com.

kind.description: Only flows of this kind: http (opened, with headers and bodies), websocket, tunnel (HTTPS passed through and only counted) or refused (the program refused FormNET's certificate, usually because it pins certificates).

limit.description: How many of the newest matching flows to return, 1 to 200.

pending.description: true for exchanges still in progress, false for finished ones; leave out for both.

q.description: Case-insensitive text found in the URL, method, status code, process name or response content type.

since.description: Only flows with a seq greater than this. Pass the highest seq of the last answer to read only what arrived after it.

tools.name: list_flows

bytes_sent.description: Bytes from the program towards the server.

client_process.description: Process name behind the client port, empty when unknown.

id.description: The flow id; pass it to get_flow.

intercepted.description: True when FormNET saw inside the exchange; false for HTTPS that was only counted.

pending.description: True while the exchange is still in progress.

seq.description: Arrival order; pass the highest one as since to read newer flows.

start.description: When the exchange began, RFC 3339 UTC.

status.description: HTTP status, 0 when there is none.

url.description: The full URL, or host:port for a tunnel.

last_seq.description: Highest seq in this answer, 0 when empty; pass it as since next time.

tools.description: Read-only. Returns one recorded exchange by id: request and response headers, timing, TLS details and the captured bodies. Use it after list_flows to read what a request actually carried or what came back. Bodies are cut to max_body_bytes (default 8192, at most 65536) and flagged truncated when cut, as text when UTF-8 and base64 otherwise. Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie and Set-Cookie values always read [redacted].

include_bodies.description: false to leave both bodies out and read only headers and timing.

max_body_bytes.description: Bytes of each body to show, 0 to 65536.

tools.title: Get one flow

tools.description: Read-only. Lists every host the proxy has seen with totals, most traffic first: flows, errors, bytes each way, first and last seen, whether anything was opened, the processes that reached it and FormNET's reading-aid label. Use it for an overview of where traffic goes before narrowing with list_flows. The label (category, owner) is a hint about the host, not a verdict.

q.description: Case-insensitive text in the host name or a process name.

tools.name: list_hosts

truncated.description: True when more hosts matched than were returned.

tools.title: List hosts

tools.description: Read-only. Returns the latest table of every connection this computer holds and the process that owns it, from the running FormNET (the same table as `formnet snapshot`). Use it to see which programs talk to the network even when they ignore the proxy. Filter by process name, pid or state (ESTABLISHED, LISTEN, ...); limit bounds both lists (default 50) and truncated says when more matched.

limit.description: Processes and connections to return, each 1 to 500.

process.description: Case-insensitive part of the process name.

state.description: Only connections in this state, such as ESTABLISHED or LISTEN.

tools.name: machine_snapshot

error.description: Why the table is incomplete, when it is.

source.description: Which tool or file produced it.

supported.description: False on a platform FormNET cannot read.

taken.description: When the table was read, RFC 3339 UTC.

truncated.description: True when more matched than were returned.

tools.title: Machine connections

tools.description: Read-only. Returns the proxy's address, whether it is listening, the interception mode (auto, on or off) and whether HTTPS is opened now, the passthrough list, the root certificate path, and the environment variables that point a program at the proxy. Use it first in any task that routes a program through FormNET, and to read back a change made with set_interception or set_passthrough.
tools.name: proxy_status

ca_path.description: The root certificate (PEM) a program must trust.

env.description: Environment variables that point a program at this proxy.

error.description: Why the proxy is not running, when it is not.

hint.description: How to use the variables, and what they do not cover.

intercept.description: True when HTTPS is opened now; false when it is tunnelled and only counted.

intercept_mode.description: auto (open HTTPS while the root is trusted), on or off.

items.description: A host or *.suffix pattern tunnelled without interception.

running.description: True while the proxy accepts connections.

tools.title: Proxy status

tools.description: Read-only. Returns FormNET's root certificate: path, common name, SHA-256 fingerprint, expiry, whether this computer trusts it, and the exact commands that trust and untrust it on this system. Use it when HTTPS is only counted, when a program refuses the certificate, or when the person asks how to trust or remove the root. Show the command for the person to run; never run it, never invent another, never ask for the private key.
tools.name: ca_info

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the certificate, hex with colons.

trust_command.description: Command the person runs to trust it.

trusted.description: True when the system trust store accepts it.

untrust_command.description: Command the person runs to remove the trust.

tools.title: Root certificate

tools.description: Writes a file. Saves the matching flows as a HAR 1.2 file under FormNET's data folder, in <data>/exports only, and returns its path; it never writes anywhere else and never replaces an existing file. Use it when the person wants a recording to open in a browser's developer tools or another HAR viewer. file_name is a plain name (letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore; .har is added), never a path. Credential headers are redacted by default. include_secrets=true writes them as captured: that is an approval choice, so ask the person before setting it. Tunnels and refused flows have no HTTP shape and are left out.

file_name.description: Plain file name for the export, such as checkout-bug.har. No folders, separators or ..

host.description: Only flows to this host: an exact name such as api.example.com, or a *.suffix pattern such as *.example.com.

include_secrets.description: Needs the person's approval. true writes Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie and Set-Cookie values as captured; false (the default) writes [redacted].

tools.title: Export HAR file

tools.description: Needs approval: destructive. Forgets every flow FormNET holds, for every program, in the web client too; it cannot be undone. Use it only when the person asks to start a clean recording. Export first with export_har if anything may be needed later.

tools.title: Clear the recording

tools.description: Needs approval: changes the proxy for every program using it, and is kept for FormNET's next start. Sets whether HTTPS is opened: auto opens it while this computer trusts the root, on opens it always, off tunnels it and only counts hosts and bytes. Use it when the person wants HTTPS contents recorded or wants interception stopped. With on and an untrusted root, programs that check certificates refuse the proxy. Returns the proxy status read back.

tools.description: Needs approval: changes the proxy for every program using it, and is kept for FormNET's next start. Replaces the whole list of hosts whose HTTPS is tunnelled without interception. Use it for programs that pin certificates (their flows show kind refused): add their hosts so they work through the proxy again, counted but not opened. Read the current list with proxy_status first and send it back with the change. Returns the proxy status read back.
